biggest_gap.what: The main quest cannot be entered or advanced by playing. Booted cold with nothing granted through the harness, 0 of 32 category:"main" quests are offerable and 32 of 32 are refused by gate.js:153 on `opens_by.topic`; `topicsKnown` is length 0 and nothing in the running world can ever add to it in the spelling the gate compares. Of the 32 AddTopic edges W1-19 appended to hooks.json, 23 seed only the topic that opens the very quest firing them (Q-MAIN-nn#10 adds the topic Q-MAIN-nn's own opens_by demands), 5 seed a topic no quest asks for, and only 4 point forward. Separately, 2 of 32 opening topics exist in the world's raw spelling at all, 0 exist as a dialogue topic id, 0 rumour lines anywhere in game/data/dialogue/** name a main-quest noun, and `opens_by.overheard_from` — declared on the three quests that are supposed to be overheard — has zero code consumers. The builder's green 29/29 trace does not contradict this: tools/quests/mainline-trace.mjs calls `H.learnTopic(step.topic)` with the exact string the gate is about to ask for, immediately before asking. Running the builder's own drop-topic sabotage — which the builder framed as a control proving the instrument can fail — is in fact the measurement of the shipping build, and it stops at Q-MAIN-01 with 0 journal entries. MEASURED VALUES BY ARTIFACT: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-19-r1/mainline-findability.json — live cold boot: main quests offerable 0/32, blocked on the topic gate 32/32, topics known at a cold start 0 || corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-19-r1/mainline-topic-supply.json — supplied only by itself 23, no supplier at all 5, supplied by something else 4 || corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-19-r1/mainline-trace.drop-topic.json — 'Q-MAIN-01: could not open — the topic "the drowned tally" has not come up yet', 0/29 and 0/17, 0 journal entries || corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-19-r1/world-coupling.json — coupling 0 on opens_by.topic, opens_by.overheard_from, q.directions and the entry_topics edges || game/src/core/topics.js — landed UNTRACKED during this measurement and states the same finding independently; it is imported by game/src/character/converse.js and NOT by game/src/sim/quest/gate.js or game/src/sim/quest/machine.js, so the fold does not reach the quest gate at commit be17753
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player who boots this build, walks to Soulrest and stands in front of Undersexton Aveline Rell cannot start the main quest, and no sentence anywhere in the world tells them the words that would let them.

remedy.action: Two edits, in this order. (1) Import `topicKey` from game/src/core/topics.js into game/src/sim/quest/gate.js and fold both sides of the two topic comparisons (line 151 prerequisite_topics, line 153 opens_by.topic) and the topicsKnown set built in machine.js context(). That alone lifts the world-suppliable count from 2/32 to 27/32 in spelling terms. (2) Re-author the AddTopic graph so it points FORWARD: each main quest's opening topic must be granted by an earlier quest's journal entry, a book, or a rumour — never by its own index 10 — and Q-MAIN-01 must have a world-side entry that owes nothing to a prior quest, which means >= 1 rumour line in game/data/dialogue/rumours.json in a settlement other than Soulrest naming the Drowned Tally, plus greeting or topic content on the three NPCs already declared in Q-MAIN-01's opens_by.overheard_from, and a consumer for that field.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/quests/mainline-findability.mjs reports `main quests offerable` >= 1 and `blocked on the topic` <= 31 at a cold start with nothing learned through the harness, AND a played run of tools/quests/mainline-trace.mjs with every H.learnTopic() call removed completes 29/29 on the intended chain and 17/17 on the backpath. Equivalently: mainline-topic-supply.json reports supplied_only_by_itself = 0 and no_supplier_at_all <= 1 (Q-MAIN-01, whose supplier must be a rumour rather than a quest).

secondary_observations.what: ELEVEN OF FORTY CHARACTER SIGNATURES CANNOT FINISH THE MAIN QUEST, and the cause is that the wave-3 clamp left exactly zero margin. Playing both chains once per (race x upbringing) signature: 29/40 complete, 11 fail. saxhleel x4 and naga x4 — the province's own two races — stop at Q-MAIN-23 in Act IV on 'salt-factor-neloth-vaun disposition 3/15' and '7/15'; dunmer/lukiul, dunmer/foreign-born and dunmer/blackrose stop at Q-MAIN-10 at quest 9 of 29 on 'rootkeeper-ashul-tei disposition 0/1'. dunmer/interior finishes, so the discriminating field is upbringing alone. The mechanism is exact and measured term by term: all nine clamped main-spine gates have a worst-signature cold-start margin of precisely 0, and the mainline's own 174 faction-reputation grants then move the derived `faction` term negative. saxhleel/interior stands at exactly 15 at the salt factor at a cold start; the FIRST quest of the main quest, Q-MAIN-01 / res_carry, takes the faction term from 0 to -12 and the standing to 3, and Act IV is shut twenty-two quests later with no route back. This is the design call the dispatch asked to be scrutinised, and the answer is that it did not preserve the authored intent: the clamp converted a permanent cold-start exclusion into a delayed one, and the offer-gate probe that certified it (tools/harness/chr-quest-race-gate.mjs) measures a cold start only and can never see it. The W1-07-r4 builder predicted this shape in its own notes ('it can close the MAIN spine on a route the player chose') and declared it out of scope; nobody re-ran the completion trace.

AR-3, seam sterility: this piece creates ZERO interactions that cross the Souls/Morrowind boundary. The full set of consequence keys across all 32 mainline quests is faction_reputation, kills_npc, locks, npc_disposition, unlocks and world_flags — nothing touches an encounter, an enemy, a spawn or a combat quantity. There is no authored encounter for the antagonist at all, so RI-QST06's requirement that 'the encounter must be authored so that [the conversation before the fight] can [happen]' has no encounter to be authored against. seam_sterile: true, justified: the piece is a quest-structure and dialogue piece by construction, but the main quest is precisely where the project's one mandatory seam crossing was supposed to live.

The two OPEN metrics the builder attributed to pre-existing content both verify, exactly. X8_foreshadowed_pct 76.92 against 80: 39 exclusive quests, 9 unforeshadowed, and all 9 are non-mainline (Q-ARCH-01, Q-SOUL-02, Q-BLAK-01, Q-STRM-01, Q-LILM-01, Q-SAP-01, Q-LEDG-01, Q-DOCK-01, Q-DEEP-01); 30 of 30 mainline exclusive quests foreshadow. silent_failure_pct 22.86 against a 5-15% band: 70 failure_states, 16 silent; the mainline's own 32 failure_states carry 4 silent = 12.50%, inside the band, and the pre-existing 38 carry 12 = 31.58%, which alone would be a hard fail. The builder's own number for its share ('4 in 45, 8.9%') uses quests as the denominator where the metric uses failure_states; the direction is right and the arithmetic is off by that substitution.

Every headline number the builder claimed reproduces on re-run of its own instrument, unmodified: intended 29/29 with 158 journal entries, backpath 17/17 with 95, 121 world flags differing between the two ending states, PONR at 0.9643 with 0 modals and 3 evidenced channels, 4/4 walk-back attempts refused, 32/32 quests with a non-violent resolution, 0 violent resolutions taken on either chain, 100% dated, 100% first person, 0 marker tokens. The census passes all five RI-QST06 hard fails. The journal prose is the strongest writing in the tree — measured against SCORING §2.2's anchors it sits at or above the 7 exemplar, carrying the giver's evasiveness and the player's suspicion rather than a stage index. None of that is in dispute; what is in dispute is that a machine walking the graph is not a player finding it.

The builder wrote tools/quests/mainline-census.mjs to close that, correctly and honestly, and I re-ran it rather than the jq. This is a corpus defect on the item, not a builder deviation.

RI-EXP05 is in a builder piece's judges list and is scoreable only at FULL tier — 20 hours of simulated play with P1 through P11. No wave-1 builder piece can satisfy that and no critic of a single piece can run it, so the item is structurally guaranteed to score 0 for W1-19 however good the endings are. self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is false in two places, both declared. RI-EXP05's Step 0 requires a FULL-tier 20-hour playthrough with P1-P11; I did not run one and scored the item 0 fail-closed on its own HF8 rather than substituting a cheaper instrument. RI-LOR01's provenance axis has no seeded-sample instrument in the tree, so I report the categorical absence of two registry entries rather than a percentage from a hand-picked list, which RI-MTH04 would void. blind_done_where_required is false: RI-QST06 and RI-JRN07 both declare blind_pair: yes, and neither pack was run — RI-QST06's blind needs an act-by-act beat table for a reference main quest with proper nouns stripped and RI-JRN07's needs a length-matched Morrowind journal sequence; neither reference artifact exists in the tree and I did not fabricate one. Both absences are recorded rather than scored as passes. Every number in this verdict came from a command listed in build.harness_commands, run by me at be17753, and every source file I opened is listed in source_reads with the demonstration that preceded it.

notes: CONSUMPTION (ARBITRATION §3 / RI-MTH07), enumerated exhaustively over W1-19's own output list, is in corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-19-r1/world-coupling.json: ten models, six with coupling 1.0 demonstrated by an entity-side observable (a gate decision or a refusal string, never a harness return value), four with coupling 0.0, and one declared unmeasured. The four zeros are opens_by.topic (orphan predicate — the gate is live and nothing in the world can satisfy it), opens_by.overheard_from (orphan data — 0 code consumers), q.directions (orphan text, RI-JRN07's fourth shape — 32 authored strings, 100% coverage, 0 ever drawn) and the 32 entry_topics AddTopic edges W1-19 appended (23 of which seed the quest that fires them). This is the ninth, tenth, eleventh and twelfth model in this project that nothing read, found by the same method that found the eighth — and the eighth was found by this piece's own builder, which is worth saying: the builder ran the audit honestly and stopped one door short, at the register rather than at the gate's other argument. The single biggest gap is the first of the four because it subsumes the rest: nothing else can be reached. AR-3: seam_sterile true, justified. Load average at the start of the run was 11.64 and peaked at 26.02; every browser run was sequential and no capture was taken.
